overall: The AG found the Carlisle ZBA did not violate the Open Meeting Law: no deliberation outside a posted meeting on the decision letter, and minutes substantially complied. Two other allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum of the ZBA deliberated outside a posted meeting by writing and signing the January 19 decision letter.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the ZBA did not deliberate outside of a posted meeting regarding the January 19 decision letter, as a quorum of the ZBA did not discuss the letter outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the December 7, 2020 and January 4, 2021 minutes were inaccurate in summarizing the appellants' position on the neighbors' businesses.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the ZBA substantially complied with the Open Meeting Law’s requirement regarding accurate and sufficiently detailed meeting minutes, and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 4, 2021 decision letter was inaccurate; the AG declined to review because accuracy of the decision is not an Open Meeting Law issue.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant's request for further review raised allegations not in the original complaint filed with the ZBA; the AG declined to review them.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to review any additional allegations contained in the request for further review that were not included in the original complaints filed with the public body.
